thread:
tess: heads-up — prod canary is showing a small but consistent latency tail on host-side for short text requests (p95 +~18%). Traces point at request parsing/tokenization step. Anyone digging in yet?

sam: saw the spike on the dashboard around 14:20 UTC. p50 stable, p95 up. Appears correlated with the runtime config flip earlier today (adaptive_batch_hint=true).

tess: minimal repro on canary with ~1000 small requests (avg payload 120 bytes). Flame shows parse/tokenize time increased from ~0.6ms to ~1.2ms for many requests. Stack excerpt:```
parse_request -> token_splitter::emit -> utf8_normalize -> memcpy
```

anjali: hmm. we changed the streaming-chunk path last week to unify on a single parse path; that introduced an extra buffer concat when frames < chunk_size. Could be a memcpy hotpath. Also want to check kernel-selection side-effects — if kernel picks a quant-friendly path it sometimes forces an extra pre-copy.

liam: ran `perf top` on canary instance, hotspot is token_splitter::emit (65% samples) and a lot of page-faults during small allocations. Quick look:```
$ perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./host-infer --replay small-requests
# perf script shows: token_splitter::emit+0x34c  memcpy+0x15  __memcpy_sse2_unaligned
```

deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-03-22T14:23 started (sha: f1e2d3c)

sam: my guess: two orthogonal regressions aligned: 1) unified parse path introduced conditional concat for streaming which allocates+copies small frames, 2) adaptive batching changed kernel selection thresholds causing different prefetch/buffer layout. Together they amplify host-side overhead.

tess: can we short-circuit the concat for single-fragment frames and reuse existing IoVecs? If so we could avoid at least one memcpy per request.

anjali: agreed. also add a kvcache metric: kvcache.slice_copies and kvcache.copy_time_ms — I suspect kvcache lookups are causing extra small buffer churn when tokenization yields many short spans.

liam: submitted a tiny patch to skip concat when fragments==1 and backing buffer is single contiguous slice: `avoid_concat_for_single_slice.patch` (PR 4123). Local microbench: p95 down ~9–11%, p99 down ~6% on the harness. Command used:```
./bench_host_parse --requests=10000 --payload-size=120 --mode=grpc_stream
# before: p95 1.24ms, p99 2.7ms
# after:  p95 1.12ms, p99 2.54ms
```

sam: applying patch to canary now. If we see tail drop we ship and follow up with a kernel-selection audit & kvcache telemetry. Can anyone add the metrics before rollout completes?

tess: I added a short unit test harness to reproduce the small-frame path and a perf CI job. Test command: `make test-parse-smallframes` — it asserts zero extra copies during parse for single-fragment requests.

anjali: also adding a quick experiment: roll back adaptive_batch_hint toggle in a secondary canary to see delta purely from batching/kernel changes. I'll create the canary and attach dashboards.

liam: noted an edge-case: when we skip concat we must ensure lifetime of pooled buffer spans entire request processing (kvcache code expects stable ownership). Added comments and a small refcount guard in the patch.

sam: :thumbsup: after canary finishes let's capture flamegraphs + kvcache hit/copy counters and re-evaluate kernel selection thresholds (sequence-length histogram vs kernel choice). If stable we promote.

tess: assigning follow-ups — postmortem if this affects >5% of traffic, add kvcache copy metrics, kernel-selection audit, and a revert plan. Thanks all, keep updates here.
